h1: Exterior Painting in Archer, FL for Homes in Full Sun
heroIntro: Archer homes often sit in open ground with no tree line to soften the sun or rain. Every step we take outside, from the first rinse to the last coat, is chosen for that kind of exposure.

sections.h2: What open ground does to an Archer exterior
body: Drive the back roads around Archer and you will see the pattern: farmhouses and ranch homes with nothing between them and the sky. That exposure is beautiful, and hard on paint. With no neighboring houses or trees for cover, the south and west elevations soak up hours of direct afternoon sun, so they chalk, fade, and crack first. Summer storms throw rain sideways across open fields, and the lowest boards near the ground pick up sandy splashback.

Meanwhile the shaded spots, like porch ceilings, the north wall, and anywhere sprinklers hit, hold moisture and turn green. A good exterior painting job in Archer, FL must cope with sunburn on one wall and mildew on the next, all on one house.

sections.h2: The exterior system, step by step
bullets: Soft wash with a mildewcide that kills growth down to its roots, so nothing spreads under fresh paint
Knock off flaking paint until only tight edges remain, then scuff any gloss so the new coat grips
Use a moisture meter on questionable boards and swap out fascia or trim that has rotted
Reset popped nails and run a flexible sealant into joints that open and close
Prime bare spots and any boards bleeding tannin
Siding and trim finished in two full coats of 100% acrylic; elastomeric over stucco with hairline cracks
Follow the sprayer with a brush or roller where the coating needs to be pushed into the surface
body: Glass, hardware, fixtures, plantings, and drives are masked before spraying. Before the crew leaves each afternoon, they hose down the landscaping.

Doors and shutters get the same attention as the siding. Front doors facing west take a beating, and a harder enamel finish keeps them looking sharp longer; see door and shutter painting for the details.

sections.h2: Timing the work around Archer weather
body: For Archer exteriors, the best months run from October to May, when the air is drier, the siding stays cooler, and storms are rarer. We can still paint in summer, but crews begin soon after sunrise and keep checking the dew point and the radar so fresh paint has time to cure before any shower. Plan on three to seven working days for a complete exterior, with washing and drying added on. Our guide to Florida painting weather explains the science.

Your Archer exterior comes with our written promise on workmanship, good for as long as 10 years, and the paint maker's own warranty still applies. If something isn't right on the final walk-around, we correct it before calling the job done, and we leave labelled leftover paint behind. If the siding is just dirty rather than failing, a soft wash in Archer may buy you more time before a repaint. Planning the whole house? See residential painting in Archer.

faqs.q: Why is my west wall peeling when the north side looks fine?
faqs.a: Afternoon sun heats and breaks down the film on west and south walls much faster. We often see chalking and cracking there years before other sides, especially on open Archer lots.

faqs.q: Can you paint in summer in Archer?
faqs.a: Yes. Summer jobs start early, and the crew lead watches dew point and incoming storms all day. Still, an Archer exterior fares best when painted between October and May.

faqs.q: Do you paint fiber-cement and wood siding differently?
faqs.a: Both get 100% acrylic, but any wood that's bare or weathered is primed first and probed for rot. Your quote names the exact product we'll use on each surface.

faqs.q: What does the exterior warranty cover?
faqs.a: The quality of our labor on the outside of your house, guaranteed in writing for up to 10 years, separate from whatever the manufacturer warrants about the paint itself.
